title: Bram and the Regiment
premise: In 1917, battlefield nurse Rafael Yarrow keeps a secret ledger recording the soldiers whose deaths officers omit from official reports, working from a requisitioned workshop that doubles as her records office. When a census taker named Bram Odell notices discrepancies in the regiment's muster rolls and asks one question too many, he is conscripted into her quiet rebellion rather than reported. As the front collapses toward their sector and a colonel moves to destroy the evidence of his falsified casualty figures, Rafael and Bram race to copy and smuggle the ledger out before the workshop is burned. Rafael escapes with the ledger at terrible cost, testifying after the armistice to restore the omitted names to their families, while Bram, wounded, survives to help her build a memorial from the pages she carried.
about_author: Yara Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records from the Great War, where she first noticed the small, deliberate gaps in official rolls. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Rafael Yarrow, a battlefield nurse at a dressing station near Ypres, begins recording in a hidden ledger the names of men whose deaths officers leave off official rolls. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief, as she measures her world in what can be carried when evacuation orders come.

chapters.title: Muster and Omission
chapters.summary: Rafael cross-references the regiment's muster rolls against her ward's dead and discovers the omissions are systematic, tied to a colonel's casualty figures. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: dawning outrage tempered by fear of what the truth could cost her.

chapters.title: The Census Taker
chapters.summary: Bram Odell, a mild census clerk seconded to the regimental records office, notices that dead men still draw pay and living men appear twice. He asks a clerk one question too many. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: naive curiosity curdling into unease as the room goes quiet around him.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Bram is summoned before a captain who offers him a choice: sign a statement retracting his query or be posted to the front line. He stalls, and that night finds a page of Rafael's ledger slipped under his door. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a fragile, dangerous resolve.

chapters.title: The Workshop
chapters.summary: Bram tracks the ledger's source to a requisitioned carpentry workshop where Rafael copies records by lamplight. They meet, wary, each testing whether the other can be trusted. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the first crack in her isolation, the terrifying relief of being believed.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael shows Bram the ledger's full scope: two hundred and six names, mothers unfound, pensions unpaid. Bram recognizes his own brother's name among the omitted. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: private grief transformed into shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Colonel Hessler, facing a board of inquiry, orders the workshop's records audited and thinned, intending to burn the discrepancy trail. Rafael learns of the audit through a sympathetic quartermaster. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: cold dread as the abstract threat becomes a date on a calendar.

chapters.title: Copying by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Rafael and Bram begin duplicating the ledger in stolen hours, Bram forging clerical cover sheets so the copies can pass as legitimate dispatches. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: fevered intimacy of shared conspiracy, exhaustion sharpening trust into something deeper.

chapters.title: A Visit from the Provost
chapters.summary: Military police search the workshop on a tip and find nothing, but Rafael's assistant Marta is detained for questioning. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: guilt and the first real price of the work, as an innocent woman pays for Rafael's secrecy.

chapters.title: Marta's Silence
chapters.summary: Bram uses his census access to locate Marta and engineer her release, burning his last reserves of goodwill with the records office. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the corruption of small compromises, doing wrong to buy time for right.

chapters.title: The Front Comes Closer
chapters.summary: The German spring offensive breaches nearby sectors; wounded flood the dressing station and evacuation of the workshop is ordered for the end of the month. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the clock she always feared, time measured now in days of light.

chapters.title: Hessler's Offer
chapters.summary: Colonel Hessler, having traced the leaks, privately offers Bram a commission and a future if he delivers the ledger and names his accomplice. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare, the seduction of power offered to a small man.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Rafael sorts the ledger into what can be carried: the names, the dates, the evidence of Hessler's signature, leaving the rest. She sews the pages into her uniform lining. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: ruthless triage, mourning the records she must abandon.

chapters.title: Bram's Answer
chapters.summary: Bram plays double agent, feeding Hessler a decoy ledger while warning Rafael that the workshop will be burned ahead of schedule, in three days. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the point of no return, fear transmuted into commitment.

chapters.title: Three Days of Light
chapters.summary: A desperate copying sprint: Marta returns to help, the workshop runs round the clock, shells fall closer each night. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: communal purpose against encroaching darkness, tenderness stolen between shifts.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Hessler's men arrive a day early. The workshop burns with most of the records inside; Marta is killed holding the door so Rafael can slip out the back. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: devastating loss, the ledger's pages literally against her heart as ash falls.

chapters.title: The Road Out
chapters.summary: Rafael and Bram flee through collapsing supply lines toward the coast, hunted as deserters, the sewn pages chafing her skin raw. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grim endurance, two people held together by what they carry.

chapters.title: Interrogation at the Port
chapters.summary: Detained at Calais as suspected spies, they face an intelligence officer who may be honest or may be Hessler's ally. Rafael must gamble on telling the truth. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the terrifying vulnerability of trust extended to an institution that has failed her before.

chapters.title: Hessler's Fall
chapters.summary: The intelligence officer verifies the ledger against independent records; Hessler is arrested as the German bombardment reaches the port. The omitted names are ordered restored. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: vindication arriving shabby and late, no triumph in it, only relief.

chapters.title: The Armistice Ledger
chapters.summary: Months later, Rafael testifies before a board of inquiry, reading names aloud until the room understands what a name is worth. Families receive the letters officers never sent. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: catharsis without closure, grief given a public shape.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Left
chapters.summary: Bram, recovering from wounds taken at the port, joins Rafael in building a memorial book from the ledger's surviving pages, each name paired with a story they gathered. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed, turning the record of the erased into something given forward.

chapters.title: Carried Forward
chapters.summary: In 1920, Rafael places the original ledger in a public archive, keeping only one copied page: her brother's name in Bram's handwriting. She measures the world now in what was carried through. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet peace, belonging found not in a place but in a shared, unerasable record.
